name: Williamina Paton Fleming
summary: Scottish-American astronomer known for stellar spectral classification and discovery of variable stars and novae at Harvard College Observatory.

name: Edward C. Pickering
summary: Physicist and director of the Harvard College Observatory who employed women computers.

name: Henry Draper
summary: Amateur astronomer who first photographed lines in stellar spectra.

name: Mary Anna Palmer Draper
summary: Widow of Henry Draper who funded the Henry Draper Memorial at Harvard.

name: Annie Jump Cannon
summary: Astronomer who succeeded Fleming and refined the Harvard spectral classification system.

name: Antonia Maury
summary: Astronomer who invented a physical classification of stellar spectra.

name: Henrietta Swann Leavitt
summary: Astronomer who discovered the Period-Luminosity Law for Cepheid variables.

name: Harvard College Observatory
summary: Astronomical research institution where Fleming worked for thirty years.

name: Harvard University
summary: University that employed Fleming and granted her official appointment.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
summary: Institution where Pickering organized the first laboratory physics course.

name: Royal Astronomical Society
summary: British society that made Fleming an honorary fellow.

name: International Solar Union
summary: Organization that adopted the Harvard spectral classification system.

name: Draper Catalogue of Stellar Spectra
summary: First extensive piece of research by an American woman astronomer, prepared by Fleming.

name: Henry Draper Catalogue
summary: Nine-volume catalogue listing spectral class of over 225,000 stars, published by 1924.

name: Henry Draper Memorial
summary: Project established at Harvard to continue Henry Draper's work in spectral photography.

name: Harvard System
summary: Spectral classification system rearranged by Cannon and adopted internationally.
